explain.say: X-rays, a year earlier! Now 1898. Marie Curie, born in Poland and working in France with Pierre Curie, found two new elements, polonium and radium. She named the effect radioactivity, which means giving out rays from inside atoms. Who named it?

explain.say: Marie Curie, yes! Next, Ernest Rutherford, from New Zealand, showed there were different rays: alpha and beta, and Paul Villard found gamma. In 1902 Rutherford and Frederick Soddy showed a radioactive atom actually turns into a different element! How many kinds of rays now?

faq.a: In 1896 Henri Becquerel found that uranium gives out invisible rays on its own, which fogged a wrapped photographic plate.
Marie Curie coined the word radioactivity. With Pierre Curie she discovered polonium and radium in 1898.

faq.q: What did Rutherford and Soddy discover?
faq.a: In 1902 they showed that radioactive decay changes atoms of one element into atoms of another element.
Paul Villard found them in 1900, and Ernest Rutherford later named them gamma rays.

faq.q: Why are Marie Curie's notebooks still radioactive?
faq.a: They are contaminated with radium, which has a half-life of about 1600 years, so it is still giving out radiation.

facts: Becquerel and Pierre and Marie Curie shared the 1903 Nobel Prize in Physics.
Marie Curie also won the 1911 Nobel Prize in Chemistry; the element curium is named after the Curies.
